channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: What Changing Your Loss Function Really Does to Gradients
item.description: Loss functions are chosen for the gradients they produce, not their formulas. A toy example shows exactly how.

item.title: Positional Encodings Versus Recurrence: Order Without Steps
item.description: Two ways to tell a model what comes before what: step-by-step recurrence, or injected positional signals. The difference shapes speed, memory, and what a model can actually learn.

item.title: How a Multi-Head Attention Block Processes One Sentence
item.description: Tracing one sentence through a multi-head attention block, step by step, with concrete numbers and no hand-waving.

item.title: Spotting a Real MLOps Certification Versus a Checklist
item.description: Most MLOps certificates test whether you can follow slides, not whether you can run a pipeline under real failure conditions. Here is how to spot the difference.

item.title: Machine Learning Salaries Versus the Actual Day Job
item.description: Job adverts sell deep learning glamour and big salaries, but most ML roles are data cleaning and stakeholder management. Learn to read the signal.

item.title: A Worked Walkthrough of Structuring and Testing a Prompt
item.description: I build a structured prompt step by step, then show how to measure whether it genuinely beat the naive version, not just felt better.

item.title: Computer Vision in Production: Why Accuracy Diverges
item.description: Demo accuracy is measured on curated frames. Shipped accuracy is measured on reality. The gap between them is predictable once you know where to look.

item.title: The Real Skill Gap After a Prompt Engineering Course
item.description: A course teaches you prompt patterns. A job teaches you that prompts fail silently, unevenly, and expensively in production.

item.title: An MLOps Tooling Decision Tree for Every Team Size
item.description: A practical guide to choosing MLOps tools by team size, with the reasoning behind each decision rather than just a tool list.

item.title: Why You Still Need Rule-Based Baselines Before Transformers
item.description: A regex or keyword baseline isn't a formality. It sets the bar a transformer must clear and reveals what your task really demands.

item.title: Deep Learning versus Machine Learning: A Worked Example
item.description: A single worked example, tabular features versus raw pixels, shows exactly where machine learning ends and deep learning begins.

item.title: Computer Vision Failure Modes Nobody Tests For
item.description: Lighting and occlusion are the easy robustness checks. The failures that actually reach production are the ones your test set never imagined.

item.title: Evaluating a Prompt the Way You Would Evaluate a Model
item.description: A prompt is a hyperparameter choice. Treat it with a held-out set, a scoring rubric, and a baseline, not vibes.

item.title: What an ML Engineer's CV Should Show Beyond a Certificate
item.description: Certificates show exposure, not capability. Here is what actually convinces a hiring manager you can do the job.

item.title: Machine Learning Glossary Disputes: One Worked Example
item.description: When teams disagree on basic ML terms, the fix isn't a dictionary, it's a worked example that forces the definitions to earn their keep.

item.title: Why Old-School NLP Preprocessing Still Matters
item.description: Modern models hide, rather than remove, the effects of classic preprocessing choices. Get them wrong and your evaluation lies to you.

item.title: Computer Vision Interviews: What They Are Really Testing
item.description: CV interview questions rarely test trivia. They test whether you understand leakage, evaluation, and trade-offs well enough to be trusted with real data.

item.title: The MLOps Job Title Spectrum: What Are You Actually?
item.description: MLOps titles are inconsistent across companies. I break down the real axes of variation so you can read a job spec instead of guessing from a label.

item.title: MLOps on a Single Machine Before You Need a Cluster
item.description: Before reaching for Kubernetes, get versioning, reproducible environments, experiment tracking and a simple pipeline right on one box.

item.title: A Practical Rubric for Scoring Prompts Before You Ship Them
item.description: A five-point rubric for judging prompts before deployment, covering clarity, robustness, grounding, failure behaviour and cost.
